games.name: Tangram Dock
games.description: Fit three unusual cargo shapes into a perfectly packed dock.
games.mechanic: polyomino packing
rules: Choose a piece, then an empty square for its top-left corner.
Fill every square without overlaps. Remove a placed piece by choosing it again.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Mirror Mail
games.description: Deliver a beam through a tiny mirrored sorting room.
games.mechanic: ray reflection
rules: Tap mirrors to turn them between / and \.
Send light from the left entrance to the bottom delivery port.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Bilateral
games.description: Restore the missing half of a woven reflection.
games.mechanic: reflection drawing
rules: The left pattern is fixed. Toggle squares on the right.
Match the exact horizontal reflection across the seam.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Shadow Turn
games.description: Turn four silhouettes until their shadows agree.
games.mechanic: independent shape rotation
rules: Each large cutout turns one quarter clockwise when tapped.
Match all four cutouts to their small reference silhouettes.
Complete all three curated studies to finish the round.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Loose Ends
games.description: Exchange crossing points to untangle a knotted necklace.
games.mechanic: graph untangling
rules: Select a point, then another point to swap their positions.
Remove every crossing between non-adjacent cords.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Gear Train
games.description: Plan three compound transmissions, from paired reducers to a locked input and a mixed-speed train.
games.mechanic: Adjacent-swap compound transmission planning
rules: Select a gear, then its neighbor in the A → B → C bench order to exchange them. Each exchange counts once; selecting the same gear again cancels. Bolted sockets cannot move.
Each mesh must meet its displayed teeth ratio: driver teeth ÷ follower teeth. Mesh ratios multiply into the output speed, but the correct final product alone is not enough.
Test the train to certify a study, then choose Next study. Finish all three. Undo reverses a swap; Reset this study keeps earlier progress; Restart begins the whole journey.
games.controls: Select adjacent bench gears by tap or keyboard Enter/Space. Test certifies a study; Undo reverses a swap. Three studies with four then six sockets.

games.name: Measured Pour
games.description: Measure a precise parcel of water with two unmarked jugs.
games.mechanic: jug transfer
rules: Fill, empty, or pour between the 3L and 5L jugs.
Leave exactly 4L in the large jug. Pours stop when full or empty.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Rover Script
games.description: Write a short route for a little delivery rover.
games.mechanic: robot programming
rules: Queue forward, left, or right commands; Run executes the route.
Collect the parcel and reach the flag without hitting walls. Clear edits your program.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Paper Trail
games.description: Fold a marked strip into one perfectly aligned stack.
games.mechanic: paper folding
rules: Fold the left or right half onto the other half.
Match the target top-to-bottom layer order after three folds.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Pigment Lab
games.description: Move translucent ink stencils to restore three layered prints.
games.mechanic: Spatial subtractive-color stencil alignment
rules: Choose a cyan, magenta or yellow stencil, then tap its top-left anchor on your print. Stencils may overlap but must fit on the paper.
Rotate turns the selected stencil clockwise and lifts it for repositioning. Match the reference, including all blank cells.
Complete three different print studies. C, M and Y letters identify inks and mixtures, so color is never the only clue.
games.controls: Tap a stencil, Rotate if needed, then a grid square. Tab and Enter / Space operate every control. Lift removes the selected stencil.

games.name: Cable Loom
games.description: Thread a cable through every brass peg in one stroke.
games.mechanic: Hamiltonian path
rules: Begin at S and tap a neighboring peg to extend the cable.
Visit every peg once, finishing at E. Undo retracts one segment.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Balance Mobile
games.description: Compose three balanced sculptures, from symmetry to fixed anchors and uneven arms.
games.mechanic: Progressive torque placement with asymmetric arms and fixed anchors
rules: Choose a free weight, then an empty hook. A hung free weight can be lifted by selecting it again. Every available weight must be used once.
Balance total left and right torque: each weight contributes its mass multiplied by its distance from the center. The sculpture tilts toward the heavier torque.
Complete three sculptures. Green anchor weights and hooks marked FIXED cannot move. Later sculptures use unequal arm distances; Restart begins all three again.
games.controls: Tap a weight and hook, or use Tab then Enter / Space. Lettered hooks show side and distance; numeric torque and tilt both reflect the arrangement.

games.name: Crate Crane
games.description: Sort a little freight yard using only its top containers.
games.mechanic: stack rearrangement
rules: Select a stack to lift its top crate, then a destination.
Stacks hold three crates. Make the left stack all A and the right stack all B.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Orbit Transfer
games.description: Navigate a one-way constellation while collecting every beacon.
games.mechanic: directed route planning
rules: Travel along an available arrow from your current station.
Collect the three beacons, then dock at F before the 8-step fuel reserve runs out.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Stamp Studio
games.description: Compose a print from overlapping transparent stamps.
games.mechanic: set union composition
rules: Toggle stamps in the tray to overlay their ink.
Match the target print. Ink only adds: extra squares cannot be erased by another stamp.
Complete all three curated studies to finish the round.
games.controls: Tap or click buttons. Tab and Enter / Space work throughout.

games.name: Minefield
games.description: Reveal the meadow without disturbing a mine.
games.mechanic: Safe-first-click minesweeper
rules: Reveal every safe square. Numbers count neighboring mines, including diagonals.
Switch to Flag to mark a suspected mine. Your first reveal is always safe.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Picross Post
games.description: A tiny picture, written in numbers.
games.mechanic: Nonogram run deduction
rules: Numbers beside each row and column describe consecutive filled runs, separated by at least one empty cell.
Tap to fill. Tap again to mark empty, then again to clear. Check when your picture is ready.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Ninefold
games.description: Four numbers. Three kinds of harmony.
games.mechanic: Mini Sudoku
rules: Fill empty cells with 1–4. Each row, column and outlined 2×2 box must contain each digit once.
Choose a digit, then a square. Given digits cannot change.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Equal Measure
games.description: Bring dark and light into balance.
games.mechanic: Binary constraint puzzle
rules: Each row and column needs two suns and two moons. Never place three identical symbols consecutively.
Every row must differ from every other row, and columns must also be unique. Tap blanks to cycle symbols.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Taller Tales
games.description: Small signs make a big difference.
games.mechanic: Futoshiki inequalities
rules: Fill each row and column with 1–4 once each.
The signs between neighboring cells point to the smaller number. Given digits are fixed.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Code Cabinet
games.description: Listen to what the lock tells you.
games.mechanic: Mastermind deduction
rules: Find a hidden code of three symbols chosen from six; symbols may repeat. You have eight guesses.
A solid dot means correct symbol and position. A hollow dot means correct symbol, wrong position. Feedback dots are unordered.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Seat at the Table
games.description: There is a place for everyone.
games.mechanic: Relational ordering
rules: Arrange five guests in seats from left to right so all written clues are true.
Choose a guest, then a seat. A guest already seated moves to the new place, swapping occupants.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Sky View
games.description: Read a skyline from every angle.
games.mechanic: Skyscraper visibility
rules: Place heights 1–4 once per row and column. A taller building hides every shorter building behind it.
Edge clues count buildings visible from that direction.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Bridgewater
games.description: Bring the islands together.
games.mechanic: Hashi bridge network
rules: Connect islands horizontally or vertically. Each island needs the number of bridges printed on it.
Tap a link to cycle zero, one or two bridges. Bridges cannot cross, and every island must join one connected network.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Loop Letter
games.description: One line. One unbroken thought.
games.mechanic: Slitherlink loop construction
rules: Draw a single closed loop along the grid edges. Each number counts the drawn edges around its cell.
Tap an edge to add or remove it. No branches, loose ends or separate loops.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Tent Pitch
games.description: Make room for a quiet night.
games.mechanic: Tents placement
rules: Place one tent beside each tree horizontally or vertically. Every tent must be paired with a different tree.
Tents cannot touch, even diagonally. Edge numbers give tents required per row and column.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Pearl Route
games.description: Give every pair its own path.
games.mechanic: Numberlink path routing
rules: Join each matching letter pair with an orthogonal path. Paths cannot overlap.
Choose a letter, then tap neighboring cells to extend its path. Tap its starting endpoint or use Clear path to start that route again. Empty cells are allowed.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Tile Weave
games.description: A quarter-turn changes everything.
games.mechanic: Pipe rotation network
rules: Rotate tiles until every pipe connects with its neighbors, with no pipe pointing outside the board.
All tiles must form one connected water network. Tap to rotate clockwise.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Safe Passage
games.description: Unpack a small traffic jam.
games.mechanic: Sliding-block escape
rules: Move the red car to the right edge to escape. Cars slide only along their length and cannot pass through one another.
Select a car, then use the arrow buttons or keyboard arrows.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Cross Sums
games.description: Let the totals do the talking.
games.mechanic: Kakuro sum intersections
rules: Fill each white square with 1–9. Row sums appear on the left; column sums appear above.
No digit may repeat within a row or column. Any arrangement satisfying every sum is accepted.
games.controls: Tap or click cells and controls; Tab then Enter / Space works throughout. Arrow keys navigate the board.

games.name: Twenty Four
games.description: Combine four cards into a single perfect 24.
games.mechanic: Pairwise expression construction
rules: Select two number cards in order, then an operation.
Each operation replaces both cards with its result. Use every card to finish at 24.
Undo lets you explore. Division by zero is never allowed.
games.controls: Tap or click two cards, then an operation. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. Undo reverses a combination.

games.name: Merge Garden
games.description: Slide a garden of numbers into one brilliant 128.
games.mechanic: Directional sliding and tile fusion
rules: Use arrows or the four direction buttons to slide every tile.
Equal neighbors merge once per move. A new 2 or 4 grows after each legal slide.
Grow a 128 tile. If every cell fills with no possible merge, start a fresh garden.
games.controls: Arrow keys slide the garden. On touch screens, use the four direction buttons. Each slide is a turn.

games.name: Bit Lanterns
games.description: Light eight little lanterns to speak in binary.
games.mechanic: Binary positional encoding
rules: Each lantern contributes the number printed above it when lit.
Toggle lanterns until their total matches the target.
Send five increasingly complex signals. Extra checks cost points, never lives.
games.controls: Tap a lantern to toggle it. Keyboard: Tab to a lantern, then Enter / Space. The total updates instantly.

games.name: Fraction Balance
games.description: Find the combination that makes both pans agree.
games.mechanic: Rational-weight composition
rules: The left pan holds the target weight. Add fraction weights to the right.
Use at most three weights; tap a weight on the pan to remove it.
Balance exactly, then check. Different combinations may work.
games.controls: Tap a fraction to place a weight; tap a weight on the pan to remove it. All controls support Tab and Enter / Space.

games.name: Matchlight
games.description: Move one match. Make the whole equation true.
games.mechanic: Seven-segment topology repair
rules: Select one dark match to lift it. Then select one empty slot to place it.
Only one match may move. All digits must remain valid seven-segment numbers.
Check the repaired equation. Undo returns the original arrangement.
games.controls: Tap a match and an empty slot, or use the Lift / Place dropdowns. Keyboard: Tab, arrow keys in dropdowns, Enter to choose.

games.name: Factor Loom
games.description: Weave prime threads into one exact product.
games.mechanic: Prime-factor resource selection
rules: Each spool is a prime number. Choose spools to multiply them together.
Each physical spool can be used once. Tap a chosen spool to return it.
Make the target product exactly. Unused spools are allowed.
games.controls: Tap a spool to weave it in or return it. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. Check when the product matches.

games.name: Clockwork
games.description: A few small jumps. One exact arrival.
games.mechanic: Modular arithmetic route planning
rules: Start at twelve. Each button moves clockwise or counterclockwise around the dial.
Land on the marked destination using exactly the allotted jumps.
Undo a jump to plan another route. Crossing twelve wraps around.
games.controls: Tap a jump button to move around the dial. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. Undo takes back one jump.

games.name: Fraction Mosaic
games.description: Fit colored pieces into a perfectly full ribbon.
games.mechanic: Ordered rational interval packing
rules: The ribbon has marked boundaries. Choose fraction pieces in the correct order.
Every placed piece must end on a marked boundary, with no gaps or overhang.
Fill the unit ribbon using the available pieces. Tap the last piece to take it back.
games.controls: Tap fraction cards to fit the ribbon in order. Remove last reverses a placement. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space.

games.name: Bracket Lab
games.description: One pair of brackets changes everything.
games.mechanic: Operator-precedence manipulation
rules: The numbers and operators stay in their printed order.
Choose the first and last number to wrap in one pair of brackets.
Make the expression equal the target. Tap endpoints again to change your selection.
games.controls: Tap two number cards to choose the bracket endpoints. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. Check the resulting expression.

games.name: Scale Sense
games.description: Find your bearings on a landscape of powers.
games.mechanic: Logarithmic magnitude estimation
rules: The line runs from 1 to 1,000. Equal distances multiply by the same factor.
Move the marker with the slider or arrow keys, then commit your estimate.
Locate five magnitudes within a factor of 1.3. A miss reveals the direction; try again.
games.controls: Drag or tap the slider. Keyboard: Tab to the slider, then left / right arrows; Home / End reach the ends. Commit when ready.

games.name: Ratio Mixer
games.description: Compose a color with just the right proportions.
games.mechanic: Integer ratio and capacity planning
rules: Add coral and teal scoops to the jar. Each scoop is one unit.
Match the requested ratio and fill the jar to its exact capacity.
Remove scoops with the minus buttons to adjust your recipe.
games.controls: Use plus / minus beside each ingredient. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. The jar shows your mixture as it fills.

games.name: Sequence Detective
games.description: A pattern is hiding in plain sight.
games.mechanic: Recurrence inference
rules: Study the visible sequence and the clue describing its family.
Choose the missing number from four candidates.
Wrong guesses give feedback. Solve five different pattern families.
games.controls: Tap or click the next number. Keyboard: Tab between choices, then Enter / Space. Read the family clue before guessing.

games.name: Exact Change
games.description: A small basket. A satisfyingly exact total.
games.mechanic: Constrained integer shopping
rules: Use plus and minus to choose quantities of three goods.
Spend the entire budget and buy exactly the stated number of items.
Prices are in cents, so your basket never suffers rounding surprises.
games.controls: Use plus / minus for each item, then Pay exactly. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. Totals use exact integer cents.

games.name: Digit Forge
games.description: Arrange a handful of digits into something precise.
games.mechanic: Digit permutation with divisibility constraints
rules: Tap digit cards to build a number from left to right.
Use each card exactly once and satisfy both clues. No leading zero.
Tap the last placed digit to return it. Check when your number is complete.
games.controls: Tap digit cards in order. Take back last lets you edit. Keyboard: Tab and Enter / Space. Check once every card is placed.

games.name: Coordinate Courier
games.description: A tiny delivery route across the Cartesian plane.
games.mechanic: Coordinate navigation with ordered waypoints
rules: Collect numbered parcels in order at their printed coordinates.
Move one grid unit with arrows or direction buttons. x increases right; y increases up.
Reach every parcel within the step budget. Undo if you take a wrong turn.
games.controls: Arrow keys or the four direction buttons move one cell. Undo takes back a step. Touch the buttons to steer.

games.name: Hidden Grove
games.description: Find four words hidden along straight lines in a leafy letter grid.
games.mechanic: word search
rules: Tap the first and last letter of a word. Lines can run horizontally, vertically or diagonally, in either direction.
Find all four listed words. A wrong line costs 10 points. Tap the same square to cancel.
Use Tab and Enter, or arrow keys within the grid. No dragging or timer.
games.controls: Tap endpoints; arrows move focus; Enter selects.

games.name: One Letter Away
games.description: Bridge two words, changing just one letter at each step.
games.mechanic: word ladder
rules: Change exactly one letter to make a word in the open notebook. All words have four letters.
Reach the target from the starting word. The notebook is the complete allowed vocabulary for this puzzle.
Submit by typing and Enter. Undo a step if you take a detour. Invalid steps cost 10 points.
games.controls: Type four letters and Enter; Undo steps.

games.name: Last Letter
games.description: Guess a hidden word before six little leaves fall.
games.mechanic: hangman
rules: Read the clue, then choose letters to uncover a hidden word.
Correct letters fill every matching position. A wrong letter costs one of six leaves. Repeating a guess is free.
Reveal the whole word to win. Six wrong letters end the round and reveal the answer.
games.controls: Tap letters or type A–Z.

games.name: Crossings
games.description: Fill three across clues and the down word that ties them together.
games.mechanic: mini crossword
rules: Fill the white squares from four clues. Three across entries share letters with one down entry.
Type a letter in each square. Arrow keys move through the board; Tab visits white squares.
Check the completed grid. Correct letters turn green; wrong checks cost 10 points.
games.controls: Type letters; arrows move; Check grid.

games.name: Wordbreak
games.description: Find the spaces hiding inside a run of letters.
games.mechanic: word segmentation
rules: Tap between letters to place or remove word boundaries.
Restore the sentence described by the clue. Capitalization and punctuation are already stripped away.
Check your spaces. Solve three phrases; wrong checks cost 10 points.
games.controls: Tap boundaries; Tab and Enter toggle.

games.name: Secret Post
games.description: Decode a letter-substitution message, one shared symbol at a time.
games.mechanic: cryptogram
rules: Every cipher letter always stands for the same plain letter. Spaces are already in place.
Select a cipher tile, then a letter from the keyboard. All copies change together; each plain letter can map only once.
Check the message or ask for a revealed letter. Hints cost 20 points; wrong checks cost 10.
games.controls: Select cipher tile, type or tap letter; Backspace clears.

games.name: Center Letter
games.description: Build five clue words around one indispensable letter.
games.mechanic: central-letter dictionary
rules: Use only the displayed letters. Letters may repeat, but the green center letter must appear in every word.
Find the five curated clue answers. This small puzzle dictionary contains exactly these five words.
Type a word and press Enter. Duplicate answers are free; other invalid guesses cost 10 points.
games.controls: Type words and Enter; five clue answers.

games.name: Odd Company
games.description: Read the relationship and find the word that does not belong.
games.mechanic: semantic classification
rules: Four words share a page; only three fit the stated relationship.
Choose the exception. A wrong choice stays on the page for another try and costs 10 points.
Solve three groups. Each reveal explains the distinction.
games.controls: Tap a word or Tab and Enter.

games.name: Alphabet Trail
games.description: Trace A to Y through an unbroken neighboring path.
games.mechanic: alphabet adjacency path
rules: Start at A and visit B, C and onward to Y. Move only one square horizontally or vertically.
Every letter is used once. Diagonal or out-of-order moves cost 10 points without changing your path.
Undo your last step if needed. Arrow keys move focus; Enter chooses a square.
games.controls: Tap cells; arrows and Enter; Undo.

games.name: Sentence Studio
games.description: Reassemble a familiar saying from shuffled whole-word slips.
games.mechanic: sentence reconstruction
rules: Tap whole words to reconstruct the familiar saying named by the clue.
The capitalized first word and punctuated last word help frame the sentence. Tap an arranged word to return it.
Check your saying. Solve three; wrong checks cost 10 points.
games.controls: Tap word slips; Tab and Enter; Clear.

games.name: Compound Works
games.description: Join two halves into four everyday compound words.
games.mechanic: compound pairing
rules: Choose a word from the left, then its partner from the right.
Every half is used once. Find the four familiar closed compound words for this set.
Correct pairs stay joined. Wrong pairs reset your selection and cost 10 points.
games.controls: Choose left then right; Tab and Enter.

games.name: Rhyme Lines
games.description: Match words by their ending sound, not their spelling.
games.mechanic: phonetic pairing
rules: Choose a word on the left and its rhyming partner on the right.
Use ordinary English pronunciation. Every word belongs to exactly one pair in this set.
Find four pairs. Wrong matches reset selection and cost 10 points.
games.controls: Choose left then right; Tab and Enter.

games.name: Vowel Weather
games.description: Bring the missing vowels back to three clue words.
games.mechanic: constrained vowel restoration
rules: Consonants stay in place. Every blank needs A, E, I, O or U.
Read the clue and type the whole restored word. Its consonants and length must match the pattern.
Restore three words. Wrong checks cost 10 points.
games.controls: Type the complete word and Enter.

games.name: Chain Reaction
games.description: Thread six words together by their first and last letters.
games.mechanic: endpoint word chaining
rules: The starting word is pinned. Choose a remaining word that begins with the last letter of the chain.
Use all six words once. Only the first and last letters matter.
Undo to escape a dead end. Invalid joins cost 10 points.
games.controls: Tap next word; Tab and Enter; Undo.

games.name: Proofreader
games.description: Spot the misspelled word and put the sentence right.
games.mechanic: spelling correction
rules: Exactly one word in each sentence has a spelling mistake. Tap that word to edit it.
Type the correctly spelled replacement and submit. The other words are already correct.
Repair three sentences. Wrong selections or corrections cost 10 points.
games.controls: Select word, type correction, Enter.

games.name: Ink & Ivory
games.description: Bracket pale discs and turn a small board in your favor.
games.mechanic: Disc-flipping territory against a three-ply positional opponent.
rules: You play ink first. Place on a dotted square so a straight line of pale discs ends at another ink disc. All bracketed discs turn ink.
The house follows the same rules. A player without a legal move passes automatically. The game ends when neither can move.
Most discs wins. Corners cannot be flipped; the house values stable corners and edges.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Four Together
games.description: Drop, threaten, block. Make an unbroken line of four.
games.mechanic: Gravity alignment against a depth-four tactical opponent.
rules: Choose a numbered column to drop an ink disc into its lowest empty space. The house then drops a pale disc.
Connect four horizontally, vertically, or diagonally to win. A full column cannot accept another disc.
A full board without a winning line is a draw. The house looks ahead for wins and threats.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Seed & Store
games.description: Sow a handful. Capture a bowl. Bring the harvest home.
games.mechanic: Six-bowl Kalah seed sowing with captures and extra turns.
rules: Choose one of your six lower bowls. Sow its seeds one at a time to the right, into your store, across the upper row to the left, then back around. Skip the house store.
Last seed in your store earns another turn. Last seed in your empty lower bowl captures that seed and any seeds in the opposite bowl, if it is occupied.
When either row empties, remaining seeds go to their owner’s store. Most stored seeds wins.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Matchstick Market
games.description: One row at a time. Leave the house without the last word.
games.mechanic: Normal-play three-heap Nim against an exact mathematical opponent.
rules: Remove any positive number of matches from one row on each turn. Buttons show row and amount.
The house removes matches by the same rule. Whoever takes the final match wins.
There is no luck. The house plays optimal Nim; the opening is winnable with careful play.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Fence & Field
games.description: A line becomes a square. A square becomes yours.
games.mechanic: Dots-and-boxes area capture with chained extra moves.
rules: Tap an empty edge between dots. Complete the fourth edge of a square to claim it.
Claiming a square earns another edge. The house captures available squares and avoids giving away easy ones.
When all nine squares are claimed, the larger collection wins.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Last Pebble
games.description: Jump a quiet garden down to one solitary stone.
games.mechanic: Seven-peg orthogonal jump solitaire on a diamond garden.
rules: Select a pebble, then a highlighted empty hole two spaces away. The pebble between them is removed.
Jumps are horizontal or vertical, never diagonal. Select another pebble to change your mind.
Leave exactly one pebble. This handcrafted arrangement has a six-jump solution; a board with no legal jumps ends the round.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Royal Crossing
games.description: Protect a path and send one pawn to the far bank.
games.mechanic: Breakthrough pawn racing with diagonal captures against lookahead AI.
rules: Select an ink pawn, then a highlighted destination. Ink moves upward one row; the house moves downward.
Move straight into an empty square, or diagonally into an empty square or an enemy pawn. Captured pawns leave the board.
Reach the opposite edge first, capture all enemy pawns, or leave the opponent with no move to win.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Hidden Fleet
games.description: Sound a little bay and account for every vessel.
games.mechanic: Battleship-style spatial search with known fleet constraints.
rules: Tap a square to sound it. A diamond marks a vessel; a cross marks open water.
The fleet contains three straight vessels of lengths 3, 2, and 2. Vessels never touch, including diagonally.
Find all seven occupied squares in as few soundings as possible. The handcrafted chart stays the same on replay.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Border Guild
games.description: Claim valuable districts. Make their shared edges count.
games.mechanic: Alternating territory drafting with adjacency and denial scoring.
rules: You and the house alternate claiming one district. Each printed number is its base influence.
Every shared horizontal or vertical edge between your districts adds 2 influence. Each edge scores once.
After all sixteen districts are claimed, most influence wins. The house weighs value, connections, and blocking your growth.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Orchard Keeper
games.description: Plan a twelve-day harvest with a small supply of rain.
games.mechanic: Deterministic resource-and-time management on nine planting plots.
rules: Plant an empty plot for 2 water. Every action advances one day and ripens planted trees by one step.
A tree is ripe after three actions, including its planting day. Tap a ripe tree to harvest 4 fruit and clear its plot. Collect rain spends a day to gain 3 water.

Gather 20 fruit in twelve days. Five plantings need more than your starting 8 water: make time to collect rain, ripen trees, and harvest. Unharvested trees do not score. Nothing advances while you are away.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Narrow Bridge
games.description: A step forward, or a fence that makes the other route longer.
games.mechanic: Pawn racing with limited route-preserving edge barriers.
rules: Your ink courier starts below; the house starts above. Reach the opposite row first. Walk one adjacent square. When facing the other courier, jump straight over it; if a wall or edge blocks that jump, step sideways around it instead.
Or choose Place a fence, then two neighboring squares. A fence blocks only their shared edge. Each side has three fences.
Fences may never remove every route to either goal. The house walks a shortest route or builds a useful detour. Sixty turns without a winner is a draw.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Sixfold
games.description: Weave a continuous thread across six-sided neighborhoods.
games.mechanic: Hex connection on a four-by-four rhombus against distance-aware AI.
rules: You place ink stones and connect top to bottom. The house places pale stones and connects left to right.
Each hex touches up to six neighbors: left, right, above, below, upper-right, and lower-left. Stones never move after placement.
The first connected chain across its two banks wins. The house takes immediate wins, blocks immediate threats, and shortens its route.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Watchtower
games.description: Three towers. Twenty-five corners to keep in sight.
games.mechanic: Queen-ray coverage optimization with a three-piece placement budget.
rules: Place three towers on the board. Each watches its complete row, column, and both diagonals. Towers do not block one another.
Dotted squares are watched. Tap a placed tower to lift it and try another square.
Cover all twenty-five squares, then Seal the plan. Partial coverage earns a score, and a complete arrangement exists.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Quiet Siege
games.description: Move your queen, close a square, and keep a corridor open.
games.mechanic: Compact Amazons territory trapping against mobility-aware AI.
rules: Your ink queen moves any distance along a clear row, column, or diagonal. Choose a highlighted destination.
Then close one empty square visible along a clear line from your new position. Closed squares stay blocked for the round.
The house does the same. Trap its queen so it has no legal move, while keeping room for your own.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Trading Day
games.description: Eight public prices. One considered trade each day.
games.mechanic: Finite-horizon inventory trading with public price calendar.
rules: Start with 12 coins and room for three crates. Each day choose to buy one crate, sell one crate, or wait.
The entire eight-day price calendar is visible. You can only buy what you can afford and sell what you hold.
After day eight, remaining crates sell automatically at the final price. Finish with at least 24 coins.
games.controls: Tap or click the board and action buttons. Tab to a control; Enter or Space selects. Arrow keys move focus between board squares.

games.name: Velvet Snake
games.description: A slow little appetite. A growing little problem.
games.mechanic: Steer a grid snake to gather twelve berries without touching walls or its own tail.
rules: Collect 12 berries to finish your garden walk.
Every berry grows your snake. Walls and your own tail end the walk.
Choose your direction early. You cannot turn straight back into yourself.
games.controls: Arrow keys or WASD; tap the four direction buttons.

games.name: Rally Club
games.description: An after-hours table for two.
games.mechanic: Paddle versus an imperfect opponent; win five points before the computer.
rules: Move your paddle to return the ball. First to five wins.
Hit nearer a paddle edge to send a sharper angle.
Your opponent reacts slowly. Change the angle to find an opening.
games.controls: Up/Down or W/S; drag on the court, or hold the direction buttons.

games.name: Paper Links
games.description: Three tiny greens. A patient line.
games.mechanic: Aim and power a friction-driven golf ball through three obstacle courses.
rules: Sink a ball on each of three miniature greens.
Drag from the ball toward your target: farther means stronger.
Use the walls to bank. Finish all greens within 12 strokes.
games.controls: Drag from the ball then release; Left/Right aim, Up/Down power, Space shoots.

games.name: Moon Basket
games.description: Put a soft arc into the evening.
games.mechanic: Adjust a ballistic shot to pass downward through a basketball hoop.
rules: Make three baskets in eight shots.
Adjust the launch angle and strength before each shot.
The ball must travel down through the hoop. A higher arc helps.
games.controls: Left/Right angle, Up/Down strength; Space or Shoot. Drag upward from the ball to aim.

games.name: Quiet Curl
games.description: Three stones. One quiet center.
games.mechanic: Aim and send three curling stones across friction ice to score proximity points.
rules: Send three stones toward the house.
A stone inside the outer ring earns points; the center earns most.
Score at least 120 total. Your stones can bump one another.
games.controls: Left/Right aim, Up/Down strength; Space or Release. Drag toward the target to aim.

games.name: Kite Flight
games.description: A ribbon of air between the rooftops.
games.mechanic: Hold-to-rise and release-to-fall flying through ten scrolling gates.
rules: Guide your kite through ten openings.
Hold Lift to rise; let go to glide down.
Touching a gate or the top/bottom ends the flight.
games.controls: Hold Space, the Lift button, or the sky; release to glide.

games.name: Soft Landing
games.description: A small engine. A softer arrival.
games.mechanic: Rotate and thrust a lunar craft, managing velocity and fuel to land safely.
rules: Land on the striped pad, upright and gently.
Use thrust to slow your descent; tilt to drift sideways.
Touch down below 32 vertical speed and 22 sideways speed, within about 13 degrees of upright.
games.controls: Left/Right rotate; hold Space or Thrust. Speed and fuel are shown below the sky.

games.name: Star Tow
games.description: Bring the strays back to their star.
games.mechanic: Steer an inertial spacecraft to pick up three cargo pods and deliver each to a central dock.
rules: Touch a gold pod to tow it. Carry one at a time.
Bring it into the central dock slowly (below 70 speed).
Deliver all three before the 60-second shift ends. Coast and brake to turn.
games.controls: Left/Right rotate, Space thrust, Down brake; use on-screen controls.

games.name: Garden Guard
games.description: A kindly eye for a busy patch.
games.mechanic: Selectively tap emerging pests while leaving flowers untouched.
rules: Tap striped pests when they emerge. Leave flowers alone.
Catch 12 pests during a 30-second shift.
Three flower taps end the shift. Missing a pest only costs time.
games.controls: Tap a garden square; keys1–9 select squares.

games.name: Beat Post
games.description: Sort the night mail to a little rhythm.
games.mechanic: Hit three lanes as scheduled notes cross a timing line.
rules: Sort 24 notes by hitting their lane at the delivery line.
Near-perfect hits earn more points. A missed note or wrong-lane / mistimed tap costs one mistake; eight mistakes end the round.
Deliver at least 18 notes. Press only the lane with an envelope at the gold line. There is no audio requirement; follow the visual pulse.
games.controls: Left/Down/Right or A/S/D; tap the three lane buttons.

games.name: Pinball Pocket
games.description: A whole arcade in your coat pocket.
games.mechanic: Operate two flippers to bounce a ball into bumpers while avoiding the drain.
rules: Light the bumpers to earn 1,000 points.
Hold the left and right flippers to bounce a low ball back up.
You have three balls. Hold one flipper while launching to aim toward that side. Side gutters stay open.
games.controls: Left/Right or A/D hold flippers; on-screen flipper buttons. Space launches a ball.

games.name: Rope Skip
games.description: A little hop. A little grace.
games.mechanic: Jump a character over periodic rope sweeps; landed recovery prevents spam.
rules: Clear 16 rope sweeps to finish.
Jump as the rope approaches your feet.
Three catches end the session. Let your feet land before jumping again.
games.controls: Space or Jump; the moving rope and countdown arc show the approach.

games.name: Table Bowls
games.description: A tidy table, a satisfying clack.
games.mechanic: Shoot a cue ball into three object balls and pocket them within eight shots.
rules: Pocket all three colored balls in eight shots.
Aim the white cue ball; drag farther for more power.
Only shoot when every ball stops. A scratched cue ball returns to the start.
games.controls: Drag from white ball; Left/Right aim, Up/Down strength, Space shoots.

games.name: Balance Beam
games.description: Keep your center while the world tilts.
games.mechanic: Lean a beam to counter a moving breeze and keep a rolling marble on the platform.
rules: Keep the marble on the beam for 30 seconds.
Tilt left or right to bring the marble back. Its weight tips the beam farther as it drifts.
Gentle corrections beat big swings. Falling off ends the balance.
games.controls: Left/Right or A/D; hold the on-screen tilt controls.

games.name: Harbor Catch
games.description: A patient line beneath the harbor.
games.mechanic: Position a boat, lower a hook into patrolling fish at different depths, then reel a catch aboard within eight casts.
rules: Land three fish within eight casts. Move the boat before you lower your line.
Hold Cast to lower the hook. Release to reel it back; a hooked fish reels in automatically.
Fish patrol different depths. Predict their path; touching the seabed wastes your cast.
games.controls: Left/Right or drag to move the boat while the hook is up. Hold Space or Cast to lower; release to reel.

games.name: Junction Nine
games.description: Keep a busy crossing flowing without letting a queue spill back.
games.mechanic: Traffic phase coordination with incompatible movements, changing arrivals and queue spillback.
rules: Choose a green phase each minute. Straight phases clear up to 5 from their queue and 1 from the matching turn queue. Turn phases clear 4 turning cars and 1 matching straight car.
Changing axis (north/south to east/west) uses one unit of clearance for safe all-red. Arrivals shown for the next three minutes join after clearance. A queue above 10 spills back and ends the shift.
Run all 16 minutes, clear at least 72 cars and finish with every queue at 7 or below. Emergency flush clears up to 3 from every queue, but you have only two.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Assembly Belt
games.description: Stamp, bake and sort a procession of little brass badges.
games.mechanic: Live conveyor processing with ordered transformations, limited machine energy and rejection handling.
rules: The belt has four stations: load → press → oven → dispatch. Every action moves every badge one station after machines operate. Load a blank of the next order’s shape or leave a gap.

A die setting stamps badges at the press; the oven must be set to bake. Changing a die or oven setting takes a tick too. The oven has 17 heat ticks; heating an empty station still costs one. The die stamps the badge already at the press before the belt moves. Ring badges require a round die; seal badges need a square die. Dispatch accepts only correctly stamped, baked badges.
Deliver at least 10 of 12 orders in 24 ticks. A rejected badge counts against the order; a gap does not. Preview the next four order shapes. Plan machine changes ahead of the moving belt.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Marsh Balance
games.description: Keep reeds, grazers and foxes in a living balance.
games.mechanic: Delayed coupled predator–prey population control with habitat regeneration.
rules: Run a marsh for 12 seasons. Reeds regrow by 8 each season, then grazers eat 1 reed each. Foxes eat up to 2 grazers each. Every third season, grazers grow by half if enough reeds remain; foxes grow by 1 if at least 6 grazers remain.

Choose one intervention each season: plant 10 reeds, relocate 3 grazers in/out, relocate 1 fox in/out, or preserve habitat (+3 reed regrowth for this season). Relocations cost 2 funds; planting costs 3. Habitat preservation is free. Every third season earns 4 funds.
Never let reeds reach 0, grazers fall below 3, or foxes fall below 1. Finish with reeds 15–50, grazers 6–18 and foxes 1–4. Birth timing means a safe-looking population can still overshoot.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Reorder Point
games.description: Order early enough, but leave room on the shelves.
games.mechanic: Inventory lot sizing with shipping lead time, holding costs and lost demand.
rules: Meet twelve days of demand. Each day choose an order of 0, 3 or 6 crates. An order placed today arrives at the start of the day after tomorrow. Two in-transit slots show exactly what is on the way.

Crates cost 2 each plus a 2-coin shipping fee per nonempty order. Each served customer pays 5. Unfilled demand is lost. Shelf space is 12; arriving overflow is discarded. Leftover stock costs 1 coin per 3 crates each night, rounded down.
Start with 8 crates and 28 coins. Serve at least 39 customers and finish with 70 coins. Orders require cash now; tomorrow’s sales cannot fund today’s order.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Workshop Shift
games.description: Three workers, a small workshop, and a very full order book.
games.mechanic: Worker placement with exclusive stations, shift resets and multi-resource recipes.
rules: Each shift has three workers. Assign one to a station; that station stays occupied until the next shift. The six stations are timber, foundry, tool bench, cart bench, training and the trading desk.

Timber/foundry produce 2 materials, plus 1 after training. A tool needs 2 timber + 1 metal and earns 3 reputation; a cart needs 3 timber + 2 metal and earns 5. Training costs 1 of each material and permanently improves gathering. The trading desk swaps 2 of either material for 2 of the other.
Finish eight shifts with 35 reputation, at least four tools and three carts. You may end a shift early, but unused workers do not carry over.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Signal Cabinet
games.description: Every job has a deadline. Every change of tools costs time.
games.mechanic: Online priority scheduling with setup costs, released jobs and completion deadlines.
rules: Eight jobs arrive during a 24-minute shift. Each needs two minutes of work. Select a released job to work one minute; switching between ink and wire tools consumes the minute as setup, without processing.
A job can be interrupted and resumed. Its remaining work stays done. Deadlines are inclusive: a job due at minute 5 must finish by the end of your fifth action. Expired jobs leave the queue.
Finish at least 7 jobs. Two missed deadlines end the shift. All release times and deadlines are public; scheduling one class in a batch saves setup but may strand an urgent job.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Cold Chain
games.description: A cool room, a warm stove, and ingredients that will not wait.
games.mechanic: Perishable batch processing with parallel aging, cooling capacity and recipe orders.
rules: Each tick brings the next pair of ingredients: F is fruit, M is milk. Warm ingredients age by one each tick and spoil at age 4. Two refrigerator slots stop aging entirely. Moving one ingredient into or out of the fridge takes a tick.

Cook jam from two fruit, yogurt from two milk, or a parfait from one fruit and milk that has chilled for at least two ticks. Parfait needs cold milk; other cooking uses the oldest suitable ingredients first, including chilled ones. A batch earns one order. Incoming ingredients arrive after aging; the kitchen holds at most 8 total. Overflow is discarded.
Across 16 ticks, make at least 3 jam, 2 yogurt and 3 parfait. Start with one fruit and one milk. Cooling can bridge a gap in the delivery schedule, but every fridge move uses cooking time.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Reservoir
games.description: Make room for rain and save enough for a dry morning.
games.mechanic: Forecast-driven release control under storage, flood and demand constraints.
rules: Fourteen days of river flow are forecast. Choose a release of 0–8 units. Today’s rain enters first; the release then leaves storage. Serve the daily demand before any excess release is counted as waste.

Storage above 20 after release floods the banks. Storage below zero is impossible: only available water releases. Each unit of unmet demand counts as a shortage. Once shortages exceed 3 the town closes the reservoir.
Finish with at most 3 shortage units, at most 13 waste units and at least 3 water in reserve. Plan storage through the dry spell, then make space for the second storm.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Power Desk
games.description: Wake the generators before the city needs them.
games.mechanic: Unit commitment with startup delays, ramping, fuel and battery dispatch.
rules: The city needs power for 14 hours. Set the slow turbine target to 0, 2, 4 or 6. Its output changes by at most 2 per hour; starting from off produces 0 on its first hour. Once started, it follows your target on later hours.

Choose battery mode with the target: reserve automatically stores up to 2 spare power or supplies up to 2 deficit; boost can supply up to 4 but never charge. The battery holds 8 and starts at 6. Each actual turbine unit costs 1 fuel.

Serve every demand with no more than 3 total unserved units, using at most 61 fuel. Finish with battery at least 2. High output is safe but wastes fuel; startup and ramping make late corrections costly.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Carry On
games.description: Pack an expedition from offers that will not come back.
games.mechanic: Sequential multidimensional knapsack with irreversible decisions and a single exchange.
rules: Twelve expedition offers arrive one at a time. Accept or pass; passed items leave for good. Carry at most 15 weight and 14 volume. You see the next two categories, but exact future sizes and values arrive with the offer.

Once per expedition you may exchange one packed item for the current offer. The removed item is lost and the exchange must fit both capacities. Different categories represent coverage, not interchangeable points.
Finish with at least 40 usefulness, four different categories, shelter and medicine. Replay uses the same expedition, so you can improve a plan with what you learned.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Quiet Majority
games.description: Find a coalition that can live with the same promise.
games.mechanic: Weighted coalition planning with permanent policy concessions, temporary grants and changing public approval thresholds.
rules: Negotiate three bills with 15 council seats. Each bill needs 11 yes votes. Harbor, Garden, Clinic and Guild have public policy weights and approval thresholds. One point of any policy helps some factions and can upset another.

Each bill allows four negotiations. Add one Harbor/Garden/Clinic policy for 1 treasury, or promise a faction a 2-point approval grant for 2 treasury. Grants expire after the vote; policy levels carry into later bills. You may vote early.

Pass all three bills and keep treasury at 0 or higher. Start with policy 1/1/1 and 12 treasury. Each passed bill returns 2 treasury; each failed bill costs 1. Thresholds change for every bill, so a first majority may not last.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Safe Return
games.description: Keep capital available for tomorrow while today’s policies settle.
games.mechanic: Collateral-constrained underwriting with overlapping policy durations, correlated claims and changing future quotes.
rules: Each day accept one insurance quote or decline. Homes cover 3 days, boats 2, farms 4, including today. Premium arrives now; every active policy pays its listed loss on every matching weather day. The complete weather and quote calendar is public.

Before accepting, free capital must cover collateral: homes 22, boats 16, farms 18. Free capital is total capital minus all active collateral. A new premium cannot fund its own collateral. Collateral is locked until that policy finishes its last daily claim check; overlapping policies compete for the same capital. Claims can push free capital below zero, but total capital must stay positive.

Start with 24 capital. In 10 days write at least 5 policies and reach the scenario’s free-capital target. Collateral still locked at closing does not count toward the target. A longer contract may block a valuable later quote. Restart repeats this scenario; choose the other scenario for a different weather and quote schedule.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away. Scenario changes start a different plan; Restart repeats the selected scenario.

games.name: Firebreak
games.description: Wind moves the fire. Give it somewhere safe to stop.
games.mechanic: Dynamic fire-front containment using persistent trenches and limited water.
rules: Protect four cabins on a 6×6 hillside for ten wind shifts. You have one crew action before each spread. A trench permanently blocks fire; water extinguishes one burning cell and all burning neighbors, but only one tank are available.

Burning cells become ash after spreading. East wind spreads east and south; south wind spreads south and west. Fire cannot cross trenches, ash or wet cells. Lightning ignites an unprotected square after spreads 3, 5, 7 and 9: respectively row 1 column 4; row 3 column 5; row 5 column 5; row 2 column 4.
Keep all four cabins unburned. Build trenches on any empty non-cabin cell. The grid labels every location and terrain; choose a burning cell for a water action. End crew turn skips remaining actions.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Kiln House
games.description: Warm the heart of the clay without cracking its shell.
games.mechanic: Coupled thermal inertia control with temperature dwell and gradient stress.
rules: Fire a clay vessel by heating both its shell and its core. Choose heat 0–3; each level spends that much fuel. Heat raises the shell quickly, while the core follows only 22% of the previous temperature gap each tick.

The shell loses 12% of its warmth above room temperature (20°) and transfers 25% of its gap to the core. Venting removes an extra 10° from the shell. A gap over 38° or shell above 110° cracks the clay.

Keep the core at 55–70° and shell at 65–90° for three consecutive ticks, then cool the core to 32° or less. Finish within 40 ticks and 30 fuel. Cooling too early resets the dwell; venting too hard can crack a hot core.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Two Couriers
games.description: Make four deliveries without sending both bicycles into one lane.
games.mechanic: Two-agent pickup-and-delivery with shared-road occupancy and parcel destinations.
rules: Two couriers share a narrow road: West gate — West junction — Center — East junction — East gate. A passing bay branches from Center; the North depot branches from West junction and South depot from East junction.

Each action moves one courier along one road. Couriers cannot occupy the same stop or pass through one another. A courier automatically picks up a waiting parcel if empty, and delivers when reaching its destination. Each carries one parcel.

Deliver all four parcels within 34 moves. The west/east parcels cross in opposite directions; use the passing bay to let loaded couriers get through. North and south parcels also cross. All positions, loads and destinations remain visible.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Elevator Night
games.description: One small lift for a building full of last-minute journeys.
games.mechanic: Capacity-constrained elevator dispatch with passenger queues and ride deadlines.
rules: Carry eight passengers through a five-floor building. Move one floor per tick, or open doors. Door opening first unloads arriving passengers, then boards the oldest waiting passengers up to capacity 2. Moving does not board or unload.

Every passenger has a release time and delivery deadline. Passengers appear at their release tick. A passenger still waiting or riding at the end of their due tick is missed and leaves. A passenger due at tick 11 must be unloaded by the end of action 11; action 12 is too late. The destination of everyone aboard is visible.
Deliver at least 7 passengers within 28 ticks. Two missed passengers end the shift. You cannot choose which passenger boards: oldest first, so route and door timing determine the load.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Supply Web
games.description: Build the little factory around its narrowest bottleneck.
games.mechanic: Production network investment with sequential material flow and throughput bottlenecks.
rules: Build a factory that turns ore into metal, timber into boards, and both into bicycles. Each tick processes stations in order: mines/forest → smelters/saws → assembly. A smelter converts 2 ore to 1 metal; a saw converts 2 timber to 1 board; assembly consumes 1 metal + 1 board for a bicycle.

Each station starts with capacity 1, except assembly capacity 0. Spend cash to add capacity, or take a contract selling up to 2 bicycles for 7 each. Production runs after every choice. Building costs: mine/forest 3, smelter/saw 4, assembly 5. Inventory carries over.
In 16 ticks, produce at least 12 bicycles and finish with 10 cash. Start with 13 cash. Extra downstream capacity is useless without raw feed, and unsold stock cannot fund construction.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Growing Block
games.description: Make a neighborhood where people want to stay.
games.mechanic: Urban zoning with spatial externalities, migration, upkeep and tax feedback.
rules: Zone a 4×4 neighborhood over twelve years. Choose a building type, then an empty lot; building advances one year. Homes cost 4, parks 3, factories 5 and shops 4. Waiting advances without building.

After each year, factories earn 3. Parks and shops each cost 1 upkeep. Homes gain one resident (capacity 4) when beside a park or shop and when adjacent parks are at least as numerous as adjacent factories. Otherwise they lose one resident. Each home pays floor(residents/2) tax; shops earn one per adjacent occupied home.

Finish with 20 residents, 8 cash and no polluted occupied home. Start with a home, park and distant factory. Shared edges count; diagonals do not. A new building’s effects apply immediately, and a negative treasury ends the plan.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Borrowed Time
games.description: Two crews and one launch date. Find the critical path.
games.mechanic: Precedence-constrained parallel project scheduling with resource-specific crew assignments.
rules: Nine project tasks form a dependency graph. Two crews work in parallel: the planner and the builder. Assign any ready task to a free crew, then advance one day. Assignment itself does not use a day.

A task cannot start until every prerequisite is complete. Matching crew specialty reduces its printed duration by one day; the other crew needs the full duration. Once assigned, a task stays with that crew until finished.
Complete Launch by the end of day 16. All tasks are required by the final dependency chain. Leaving a crew idle can be correct when tomorrow unlocks a task it handles faster.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away.

games.name: Convoy Ledger
games.description: Protect today’s cargo without stranding tomorrow’s escorts.
games.mechanic: Multi-wave escort dispatch with simultaneous lane packing, voyage return times and permanent casualties.
rules: Seven waves each have three cargo lanes. Assign your six escorts, then sail all lanes together. A lane delivers only if assigned escorts meet its printed threat. Assignments can be recalled until sailing. The full threat, cargo and trip-length calendar is public.

A protected lane delivers its cargo immediately, but its escorts stay away for the printed number of waves, including the departure wave. A 1-wave trip returns before the next allocation; a 3-wave trip skips the next two allocations. The return ledger shows exactly when escorts come home. Escorts cannot serve two lanes at once.

Meet the scenario’s cargo target in seven waves. There are no replacement escorts. Underprotected lanes lose all cargo and one assigned escort permanently; the others return after that lane’s trip. Partial cover offers no cargo benefit, so abandon a lane with zero escorts if you cannot protect it. Long voyages can deny protection to tomorrow’s more valuable cargo. Restart repeats the scenario; the other scenario changes trip priorities.
games.controls: Tap the labeled actions, or use Tab and Enter / Space. Arrow keys move between actions. Nothing advances while you are away. Scenario changes start a different plan; Restart repeats the selected scenario.

games.name: Velvet Tricks
games.description: Follow suit, save a trump, and take control of the lead.
games.mechanic: Follow-suit trump trick taking with a changing leader.
rules: Play one card per trick. You must follow the lead suit if you can; otherwise any card is legal. Spades are trump. Highest trump wins; without trump, highest card of the lead suit wins.
The trick winner leads next. Your eight-card hand and the house hand exhaust together. Win at least five tricks; four is a draw. The house conserves high cards when it cannot win.
games.controls: Tap or click cards, board squares and labeled actions. Tab moves focus; Enter or Space activates. Arrow keys move between neighboring controls. No timing or dragging required.

games.name: Twenty-One
games.description: Read the dealer. Decide how much of your stack belongs on the next card.
games.mechanic: Five-round blackjack with hit, stand, double and a finite chip stack.
rules: Start with 20 chips. Each of five hands costs a 2-chip stake. Aces count 11 or 1; faces count 10. The dealer shows one card and stands at 17, including soft 17.

Hit for another card or stand. Double is available only on your first decision, costs another 2 chips and deals exactly one card. Above 21 loses. A two-card 21 pays 3:2; other wins pay 1:1.
